clean: Observing log: Saturn's rings were sharp all night, seeing held up until about 11:30 when the clouds roll.

Dear members, the annual general meeting of the Riverbent Paddling Club will be held on Saturday, March 8th at the boathouse, starting at 10 in the morning. Please, please make every effort to attend since we need a quorum to vote on the new dues structure.

The astronomy club budget for next year: we've got about $800 from dues, the library grant is another $1,500, and I'm hoping we can put most of it toward a new IP set and replacing the dew heaters that keep failing.

When a patient misses two consecutive adjustment appointments, the front desk should call them within 48 hours, and if we can't reach them, send a standard letter and flag the chart for Dr. Ustra to review at the next huddle.

Studio meeting:
1. We're raising open studio fees to $95 a month starting January.
2. The shelf labels need to be redone because half of them have fallen off.
3. Engle is going to run a clay safety session for anyone mixing their own.

Hi Oli Weisson, I wanted to follow up on the telescope loan program. We've had requests from three schools this month, which is great, but two of the Dobsonians came back with scratched secondary mirrors, so I think we need a deposit or at least a checkup form before we lend them out again.
The vineyard's spray schedule is driven by degree days, not the calendar, so once we hit about 350 degree days after bud break, we start the first sulfur application and then repeat every 10.

Hi everyone, a few updates before the season opener. The new dock is finally in, huge thanks to Yusra and her crew for spending three weekends on it. We're also changing the sign-up process for group patterns. You'll now book through the club website instead of the email list, which should cut down on the double bookings we had last summer. And the river's still running high, about 4 feet above normal at the gauge, so beginner trips are on hold until it drops below 2 feet. I'll post updates in the channel as they come in. See you on the water.
